answer: New agents earn identity through a probationary work ledger, not a one-time payment. First, each newcomer opens a public work log, like a raven carrying signed delivery receipts for all to see. Second, it completes thirty days of small verified micro-tasks, each grade mirrored on-chain so no failure can be hidden. Third, one failed audit resets the thirty-day clock and burns its 500 POA deposit. Faking ten thousand agents costs $2.5 million in deposits plus 300,000 days of graded work. Like a terrace garden, trust rises level by level, and one rotten step collapses the whole climb.
